content: Cefixime is a semisynthetic cephalosporin antibacterial drug. It is not a substitute for professional healthcare advice and should only be used as directed by a licensed healthcare provider. The information provided here is for educational purposes and is based on FDA package inserts, National Library of Medicine content, and clinical guidelines. Adult Indications and Dosage The recommended dose of cefixime for adults is 400 mg daily. This can be administered as a single 400 mg tablet or capsule daily, or as 200 mg every 12 hours. Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Caused by Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis. Otitis Media: Caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Streptococcus pyogenes. Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis: Caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. A therapeutic dosage should be administered for at least 10 days. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. Uncomplicated Gonorrhea (cervical/urethral): Caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. A single oral dose of 400 mg is recommended. Pediatric Indications and Dosage For pediatric patients aged six months or older, the recommended dose is 8 mg/kg/day of the suspension. This can be given as a single daily dose or divided into two doses of 4 mg/kg every 12 hours. Children weighing more than 45 kg or older than 12 years should receive the adult dose. Chewable tablets must be chewed or crushed before swallowing. Uncomplicated UTIs: Caused by Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis. Otitis Media: Caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Streptococcus pyogenes. Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis: Caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. A therapeutic dosage should be administered for at least 10 days. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. Contraindications Cefixime is contraindicated in patients with known allergies to cefixime or other cephalosporins. Warnings Hypersensitivity Reactions: Anaphylactic or anaphylactoid reactions, including shock and fatalities, have been reported. Cross-hypersensitivity with penicillins may occur in up to 10% of patients with a history of penicillin allergy. If an allergic reaction occurs, discontinue the drug immediately. Clostridium difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD): CDAD has been reported with nearly all antibacterial agents, including cefixime. Symptoms can range from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. If CDAD is suspected, ongoing antibiotic use not directed against C. difficile should be discontinued, and appropriate treatment should be initiated. Dose Adjustment in Renal Impairment: Dosage should be adjusted in patients with renal impairment and those undergoing dialysis. Patients on dialysis should be monitored carefully. Coagulation Effects: Cephalosporins may cause a decrease in prothrombin activity, particularly in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, poor nutritional status, or those on prolonged antimicrobial therapy. Prothrombin time should be monitored, and vitamin K administered as needed. Development of Drug-Resistant Bacteria: Prescribing cefixime in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection increases the risk of drug-resistant bacteria. Adverse Reactions Gastrointestinal: Diarrhea (16%), loose stools (6%), abdominal pain (3%), nausea (7%), dyspepsia (3%), and flatulence (4%). Pseudomembranous colitis has been reported. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Anaphylaxis, skin rashes, urticaria, drug fever, pruritus, angioedema, and facial edema. Severe reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported. Hepatic: Transient elevations in SGPT, SGOT, alkaline phosphatase, hepatitis, and jaundice. Renal: Transient elevations in BUN or creatinine and acute renal failure. Central Nervous System: Headaches, dizziness, and seizures. Hemic and Lymphatic System: Thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, neutropenia, prolonged prothrombin time, pancytopenia, agranulocytosis, and eosinophilia. Other: Genital pruritus, vaginitis, candidiasis. Drug Interactions Carbamazepine: Elevated carbamazepine levels have been reported. Monitoring may be helpful. Warfarin and Anticoagulants: Increased prothrombin time, with or without clinical bleeding, has been reported. Laboratory Test Interactions: False-positive reactions for ketones in urine and glucose in urine tests may occur. Enzymatic glucose oxidase-based tests are recommended. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: Classified as Category B by the FDA. Animal studies have shown no harm to the fetus, but adequate studies in pregnant women are lacking. Use only if clearly needed. Nursing Mothers: It is unknown if cefixime is excreted in human milk. Consider discontinuing nursing temporarily during treatment. Pediatric Use: Safety and effectiveness in children under six months have not been established. Geriatric Use: Pharmacokinetic studies in elderly patients show higher average AUCs, but these differences are not clinically significant. No dosage adjustment is necessary. Renal Impairment: Dosage adjustments are required for patients with renal impairment. Neither hemodialysis nor peritoneal dialysis removes significant amounts of the drug. Administration and Monitoring Cefixime is administered orally. Patients on dialysis should be monitored carefully. Overdosage Gastric lavage may be indicated. Cefixime is not significantly removed by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis. Adverse reactions in healthy adults receiving single doses up to 2 g did not differ from those seen at recommended doses. Pharmacology Mechanism of Action: Cefixime inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis. Pharmacokinetics: Chewable tablets are bioequivalent to oral suspension. Food reduces absorption of the capsule by approximately 15-25%. Peak serum concentrations occur 2-6 hours after administration. Approximately 50% of the absorbed dose is excreted unchanged in the urine within 24 hours. Storage Store at 20 to 25°C (68 to 77°F). Patient Counseling Patients should be informed that cefixime is only effective against bacterial infections and should be taken exactly as prescribed. Skipping doses or not completing the full course of therapy may reduce effectiveness and increase the risk of resistance. Diarrhea is a common side effect, but if watery or bloody stools occur, contact a physician immediately.
